ORAL JUDGMENT This appeal by the owner of the vehicle challenging the judgment and award dated 14.01.2015 in MVC No.637/2012 passed by the Additional Senior Civil Judge & JMFC, Additional MACT-12,
Bhadravathi, ('the Tribunal' for short) fastening the liability against him to pay the entire compensation.

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, rank of the parties will be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 08.05.2012 at about 8:20 P.M., the son of the petitioners by name Sunil @ Sunil NC: 2024:KHC:32449 Naik, the deceased, while travelling in a luggage tracks bearing Registration No.KA-15/6536 was met with an accident at Varthegundi village of Tarikere Taluk.

Due to which, he fell down and sustained head injuries and he was admitted to Mc.Gann Hospital,
Shivamogga where he succumbed to death.
Petitioners being the dependents approached the Tribunal seeking compensation.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company and owner of the vehicle.
After taking the evidence and hearing both parties, the Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.3,32,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a., directing the owner of the vehicle to satisfy the award.
Aggrieved by the same, the owner of the vehicle is before this court.

sentences.text: 4. Heard the argument of Shri Chandrashekar, learned counsel for the owner of the vehicle and Shri C.R.Ravishankar, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.

5. It is contended by learned counsel for the owner of the vehicle that the original insurance policy has been produced before this court and also before the Tribunal to explain that there is a valid insurance cover for a period 21.06.2011 to 20.06.2012.
Owner of the vehicle himself was driving the NC: 2024:KHC:32449 vehicle and he was holding a valid driving license to drive the said category of vehicle.

He further contended that the deceased being 'loader', there is a coverage in the insurance policy and the Insurance Company has to indemnify the owner but the Tribunal erroneously mistook the facts and directed the owner to pay the compensation exonerating the Insurance Company.
6.

Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company contended that there is a valid policy issued covering the period of accident but the deceased was passenger in the goods vehicle and the policy of the Insurance will not cover the risk of the deceased and for this reason, the Tribunal has directed the owner of the vehicle to pay the compensation and he supported the impugned judgment.
7.
I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed by the learned counsel for both parties and perused the records.
8. Respondents No.1 and 2 in this appeal are the petitioners.

Though they are served with the notice,
they have remained absent.
The question before this court is liability on the part of the Insurance Company to indemnify the insured.

Copy of the Insurance Policy clearly points out that on the date of accident i.e., 08.05.2012,
it was in force.
The owner himself is the driver of the vehicle and he was holding a valid driving license at the time of accident.
When the driver is holding a valid driving license and there is Insurance policy, the Insurance Company can avoid its liability?
The Insurance Company has collected premium for a non-fare paying passenger.
Policy of Insurance covers coolie as well as the non-fare paying passenger.

Even if the deceased is taken as non-fare paying passenger or a coolie,
policy covers the risk.
Under such circumstances, the Insurance Company has to indemnify the insured.
Hence, the Insurance Company cannot avoid its liability to pay compensation.
The Tribunal erroneously exonerated the Insurance Company, which needs interference.
